rationale: This is a correct four-phase handshake. req and ack each cross through two stages. The source latches the payload only when !src_req && !a2 and holds it until the synchronised ack, then drops req. The destination captures exactly once (r2 && !ack_dst) and drops ack only after r2 falls. The next transaction waits for a2 to go low. Nominal sequencing gives single delivery of a coherent payload. The parent intake bench ran to $finish with no assertion errors.
caveats: A single-transaction bench does not prove repeated transactions, liveness or reset sequencing.

Both domains release from raw rst_n. Simultaneous asynchronous assertion with independent release looks benign: a request issued before the destination leaves reset is held until r1 samples it. RDC-023 (handshake reset-release order) and RDC-003 still apply as obligations.

Expected non-defect findings are CDC-015 INFO, a CDC-024 WARNING obligation, a CDC-039 WARNING obligation and RDC-023. The case is a good control that requires review, not a clean one. No whole-IP clean premise. Raw rst_n asynchronously resets every register with no local release synchroniser and no SDC reset exception; RDC-003 (WARNING Unresolved), RDC-002 (WARNING Unresolved) and RDC-013 (physical obligation) are expected if RDC rules run. The contract states only asynchronous assertion, so this is a whole-IP premise gap, not a defect of the labelled crossing.

author_reading.rationale: Source asserts send to latch payload into a source-domain holding register, holds request and data until synchronized acknowledgment, then drops request. Destination captures once while request is synchronized high and returns acknowledgment; source waits for acknowledgment low before retriggering. Independent bench checks a single delivered transaction and coherent payload.
limitations: Structural attribution is a proposal for independent adjudication, not analyzer outcome.
Physical timing and metastability requirements remain external.
